rationale.usefulness: The six-phase workflow, stable coverage ledger and distinct confirmed/needs_validation/rejected records can make agent audit output easier for application builders to reproduce and act on. The report translates that into bounded classroom, app-export, upload-preview and video-job exercises without claiming tested integrations; demanding host isolation limits immediate adoption.
rationale.impact: Source-grounded validation, explicit unfinished coverage and fresh record verification address a meaningful reliability problem in AI-assisted security review. This is a reusable workflow contribution within a domain, not measured improvement in vulnerability discovery or false-positive rates, and correlated model errors remain possible.
rationale.novelty: The contribution is the concrete integration of coverage accounting, isolated hunting, adversarial validation and schema-based reporting. These are established security/review principles in an inspectable agent workflow, with no comparative evidence of a fundamentally new auditing method.
rationale.maturity: The README and companion documents specify operating profiles, prerequisites, output contracts and validators clearly enough to support a controlled pilot. The evaluator has not run the validators or the workflow, reviewed all attack-domain files or shown host enforcement, so documentation completeness is not equivalent to demonstrated audit effectiveness.
rationale.openness: The actual MIT text permits broad reuse, modification and distribution with notice retention, and the workflow, companion instructions, schemas and validators are available in the repository. External model and sandbox dependencies remain outside that license; full experimental reproducibility and all implementation behavior were not verified, which prevents a perfect score.
